clue.text: Most certainly a source of comfort when drought threatens

definitions.meaning: to know something this way is to be quite sure of it

definitions.text: a source of comfort when drought threatens
definitions.meaning: a brimming water source is reassuring in a dry spell

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the idiom in 'you know it full well'; the second reads the phrase literally as a well that is not dry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means beyond doubt, while literally a brimming well keeps water flowing in a dry season.

clue.text: Why inspect a horse's teeth only to find horse food?

definitions.meaning: dealers look at a horse's teeth to judge how old it is, read as two words giving the reason
fodder such as hay given to horses

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words the answer gives the reason for checking teeth: horses' teeth show their years.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word gives the reason for checking teeth; whole it means fodder for livestock.

clue.text: It puts a gloss on Ulster disturbance

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A commentator puts a positive spin on unrest in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is a province mostly in Northern Ireland, and 'disturbance' recalls the Troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen or shine is what a gloss gives a surface.

clue.text: Ex PM who had to win around a capital orchestra

indicators.note: around has the victory word wrapped about the orchestra

parts.note: taken as written
the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra, based in the capital

explanation.surface: A former prime minister had to win over a London orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Wilson was a Labour prime minister of Britain in the 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Wilson was twice Britain's Labour prime minister, so a former premier.

clue.text: Cabinet had insufficient freedom of manoeuvre

definitions.meaning: a cabinet can be a small private room
having scant space or scope to act

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests government, but here it is its old sense of a small chamber. 'had' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet was historically a small private chamber; figuratively, scant scope is not much space to act.

clue.text: RM ship ordered to find shellfish

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Royal Marines vessel is sent off in search of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: RM looks like the Royal Marines but is just two letters of fodder for 'ordered'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crustacean caught for eating is one kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Arrested because quantity of drugs seized led to noted racket

parts.note: a haul is a quantity of seized goods
E is a musical note, so noted contributes a note
din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: Someone was arrested after a drugs seizure led to a famous scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like a criminal scheme next to drugs, but it is noise; 'noted' adds a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Police taking a suspect into custody bring them in to the station.

clue.text: Popular with pepper and salt when you can buy game

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to season food is to add pepper and salt

explanation.surface: Shoppers favour well-seasoned game when it is available.
explanation.definitionFit: Game birds and venison may only be sold during the permitted shooting period of the year.

clue.text: Naturally enough boys think it is for writing carved initials

definitions.text: Naturally enough boys think it is for writing carved initials

parts.words: Naturally enough boys think it is for writing carved initials
parts.note: the small folding blade was originally for cutting quill pens, but schoolboys use it to cut their initials into desks

explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from sharpening quills for writing; the clue jokes that boys take 'writing' to mean carving initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The small folding blade was named for trimming quill pens, the writing link.

clue.text: Stringed instrument following two notes without a quaver

indicators.note: following places the instrument after the two notes in the answer

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
so (soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musician describes a lute piece played after two notes, with no tremble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quaver' looks musical but here means a tremble of nerves: someone without a quaver is firm and determined.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shows no tremor of doubt is firm and determined.

clue.text: What the weaving road hog does to reduce transgression

definitions.text: What the weaving road hog does

parts.note: to cut something is to reduce it
a sin is a transgression

explanation.surface: A reckless driver weaves through traffic while someone talks of curbing wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver who swerves in front of others pushes into the line of traffic ahead of them.

clue.text: A grey log carved as a hideous face

indicators.note: carved suggests wood cut into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woodcarver turns a grey log into a grotesque head.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque carved head, often a waterspout on a church, is a classic hideous face.

clue.text: In wet weather mutton (typically) should not go off

indicators.note: in puts the measure inside the weather word

parts.note: rain is wet weather
in printing an em space is called a mutton, so mutton gives EM

explanation.surface: A farmer warns that meat left out in the rain must not spoil.
explanation.walkthrough: Printers called an em quad a 'mutton' to tell it apart from the en ('nut'). The definition is verbal: to stay put is not to go off.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put is not to leave or depart, a synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: Soak soft Basmati, though it is expensive!

definitions.note: the adjective stands for a noun phrase naming a high cost

parts.note: to steep is to soak
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
basmati is a variety of rice

explanation.surface: A cook soaks basmati to soften it, grumbling about the cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A high cost charged for something is what makes it dear.

clue.text: Send letter to one dandy to cancel the debt

parts.note: to write is to send someone a letter
I is the Roman numeral for one
a toff is a well-dressed, upper-class man, a dandy

explanation.surface: Someone drafts a letter to a fashionable gent asking him to forget what he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a posh, smartly dressed person.
explanation.definitionFit: Accountants record an unrecoverable sum as a loss, giving up the claim on it.

clue.text: When snuff takers sneeze if absolutely necessary

definitions.meaning: snuff is taken in small pinches, which can provoke a sneeze
in an emergency, only if needed

explanation.walkthrough: Snuff is powdered tobacco sniffed in small pinches between finger and thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: Snuff users sneeze on taking a pinch; the idiom means only if needed.

clue.text: Captains look for ship full of herring

indicators.note: full of puts the fish inside the ship

parts.note: SS (steamship) is the abbreviation for a ship
a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: Ship's masters look for a vessel loaded with herring.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a split, smoked herring, a British breakfast dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The masters of ships or leaders of teams are captains.

clue.text: A hit to the leg side results in being out!

indicators.note: to joins the side word ahead of the hit word in the answer

parts.note: in cricket the on side is the leg side
a strike is a hit

explanation.surface: A cricket shot to leg ends in the batsman being dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like dismissal in cricket but means workers walking out. The on (leg) side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who withdraw their labour in a dispute are said to be out.

clue.text: Relieving one's bowling partner?

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls; a bowler who replaces a team-mate at that end is literally receiving the next set of six

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket bowlers alternate overs (sets of six deliveries); the phrase both means replacing someone and, literally, receiving the over to bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming another person's duties is relieving them, and in cricket it is literally getting the over.

clue.text: It disperses smoke from oil containing double nitrogen

indicators.note: containing has the oil word hold the nitrogen pair

parts.note: oil is a fuel

indicators.note: double here means the nitrogen symbol appears twice over

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chimney carries off smoke from burning oil laced with nitrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's or engine's smokestack carries the smoke away and up into the air.

clue.text: Sheep doctor goes around Ireland

indicators.note: goes around has the doctor wrap the island

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A vet travels about Ireland treating sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of fine-wooled sheep, originally from Spain.

clue.text: Herpes spreading around the globe

indicators.note: spreading suggests things scattered out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A virus spreads across the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball or orb is a round solid, a synonym for globe.

clue.text: Change from grub the little dog made a meal of

parts.note: a pup is a young or little dog
to eat something is to make a meal of it

explanation.surface: A puppy wolfs down some food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food, which fits the dog's meal, but it is a larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva becomes a chrysalis before emerging as an adult insect, the stage between grub and butterfly.

clue.text: Get smart when the forest seedling has sprouted

definitions.meaning: to make oneself tidy and well turned out

definitions.text: when the forest seedling has sprouted
definitions.meaning: read literally, a young conifer has come up through the soil

explanation.definitionFit: Tidying one's appearance is the idiom; literally a young conifer of that type has come above ground.

clue.text: Relating to a mind once it is disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist observes that a mind, once troubled, stays affected.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, from Greek nous, describes things belonging to the intellect.

clue.text: VIP-one taken in by Cyrano de Bergerac's prominence

indicators.note: taken in by puts the numeral inside the facial feature

parts.note: Cyrano de Bergerac, the hero of Rostand's play, is famous for his very large nose
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An important figure is fooled by the famous nose of Rostand's hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prominence' sounds like fame, matching VIP, but it is a protruding feature.
explanation.definitionFit: An important, influential person is colloquially called this.

clue.text: Having reached double figures, get a move on

parts.note: having becomes has as in 'he has'
ten is the first number in double figures

explanation.surface: A child turning ten is told to hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry is to move faster, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Touch on an angry spot or be touched on it

definitions.meaning: literally to touch an inflamed patch of skin
to be touched on a sensitive matter, to be aggrieved or resentful

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal (to feel a sore); the second is to be resentful, touched on a raw nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one probes a painful lesion; figuratively one is resentful after a sensitive matter is raised.
